Rust pretends the returned slice is 'static

explanation: No 'static claim is made; the compiler derives the input-output link.

q: Why is a `&mut T` borrow called exclusive?
options: While it exists, no other borrow of the same data may coexist — one writer or many readers
It must be the last borrow ever taken on the value
It can only be held in a single thread forever
The compiler takes exclusive access for the borrow's scope, then requires it to end before other access
explanation: Later borrows are allowed once the &mut ends.
&mut is about that moment's access; threading is a separate question.
Exclusivity is enforced at compile time, not negotiated at runtime.
